definitions.explanation: The act of entering a restricted or prohibited area. Most commonly seen in prohibition signs and warnings.

examples.japanese: {工事中|こうじちゅう}のため、{立|た}ち{入|い}りはご{遠慮|えんりょ}ください。
examples.english: Please refrain from entering, as construction is underway.

examples.japanese: {許可|きょか}なく{敷地|しきち}に{立|た}ち{入|い}ると、{法律|ほうりつ}で{罰|ばっ}せられることがある。
examples.english: Entering the premises without permission may be punishable by law.
examples.notes: Here {立|た}ち{入|い}る is used as a verb rather than the noun form.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立|た}ち{入|い}り{禁止|きんし}: no entry, keep out
- {立|た}ち{入|い}り{検査|けんさ}: on-site inspection
- {立|た}ち{入|い}り{調査|ちょうさ}: on-site investigation

VERB FORM:
The verb form is {立|た}ち{入|い}る (to enter, to trespass). This noun form is the masu-stem nominalization.

USAGE:
Most frequently encountered on signs ({立|た}ち{入|い}り{禁止|きんし}) and in formal or legal contexts.
